blocks.text: For some, getting a new iPhone means capturing life’s best moments. For others, it means finding smarter ways to work, stay connected, and make everyday life easier.

blocks.caption: A NIGHT TO GO PRO. Smart executives and guests celebrate the arrival of the iPhone 18 Pro at Smart’s flagship store in SM Megamall, bringing together technology enthusiasts and subscribers for a night of excitement, entertainment, and a first look at Apple’s latest flagship device.

blocks.text: These reasons came together as Smart Communications, Inc. (Smart) welcomed the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max with a nationwide midnight launch led by its flagship store at SM Megamall in Mandaluyong City.

The celebration brought together subscribers, tech enthusiasts, and Apple fans for a night of live performances, interactive games, and a synchronized midnight reveal at Smart Stores in SM Davao, SM Clark, SM City Dasmariñas, and SM Southmall, with live video check-ins connecting subscribers across the country.

blocks.caption: MADE TO GO PRO. The iPhone 18 Pro takes center stage at Smart’s nationwide midnight launch.

blocks.text: An upgrade worth staying up for

Among the first in line was Geneva Santos, a mother of three and loyal Smart Postpaid subscriber since 2010. Wearing a green coat over a burgundy top, she arrived ready to welcome the new flagship in style, choosing the upgrade primarily for work.
“I’m really satisfied with Smart Postpaid,” Santos shared, citing the service and customer support she has experienced over the years.
“I appreciate getting a reminder that my current plan was nearing its end, making my upgrade very timely and convenient. Smart Postpaid’s installment options are easier on the pocket,” she added.

For Edgardo Red, Jr., a customer success specialist and Smart subscriber for 13 years, the midnight launch was a first. Although his family regularly upgrades their phones, he wanted to experience the excitement of welcoming Apple’s latest device firsthand.

“What I’m really looking forward to with the iPhone 18 Pro is how it integrates artificial intelligence into the device itself, making it more convenient for the user,” said Red, who chose the Burgundy variant.
18 reasons to go Pro with Smart
Beyond the excitement of getting a new device, Smart highlighted how subscribers can get more out of their iPhone 18 Pro through Smart Postpaid Plans+.

In his remarks, Lloyd Manaloto, First Vice President and Officer-in-Charge of Smart, presented 18 reasons to pair the latest iPhone with Smart, drawing inspiration from the years of innovation since the original iPhone transformed the mobile industry.

blocks.caption: MORE REASONS TO GO PRO WITH SMART. Lloyd R Manaloto, First Vice President and Officer-in-Charge of Smart, highlights the benefits of pairing the iPhone 18 Pro with Smart Postpaid Plans+, giving subscribers more ways to enjoy Apple’s latest flagship through flexible payment options and exclusive p…

blocks.text: “We make it so much easier for you to get the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max with our postpaid plans,” Manaloto said. Under Smart Postpaid Plans+ 1499, subscribers were able to pre-order the former for only P3,713 per month and the latter for P4,050 per month.

Eligible subscribers also received 18GB of complimentary open-access data for pre-orders, a P5,000 accessory voucher, an 18% discount on select Digimap accessories, and 5% bill cashback when paying through the LiveSmart App.

As part of their plan, Smart subscribers also enjoy unlimited access to an app bundle, Unli 5G connectivity for 12 months, all-net calls and texts, landline calls, and dedicated network priority. Open-line devices also offer flexibility for international travel and compatible dual-eSIM setups.

The Smart Postpaid experience extends across the digital ecosystem, with a complimentary subscription to AI.Smart, Apple Pay functionality, and Smart Device Link service, which allows subscribers to share their primary iPhone mobile number and data plan with their compatible Apple Watch.

On top of these benefits, subscribers can make the most of the latest iPhones on Smart’s award-winning network, which was recently recognized by Ookla for delivering the Philippines’ Best Mobile Video Experience.

articles.title: Merchants can scan unified digital PWD cards for verification --NCDA
articles.summary: The National Council on Disability Affairs (NCDA) said that merchants can scan the newly established unified digital ID to verify its authenticity. However, it stressed that a presumption of…

blocks.text: Published November 11, 2026 6:11pm

The National Council on Disability Affairs (NCDA) said that merchants can scan the newly established unified digital ID to verify its authenticity. However, it stressed that a presumption of regularity should still apply to persons with disabilities (PWD).

The NCDA is rolling out its Unified PWD Identification System (UPWDIS), which is a centralized platform to curb fraudulent PWD cards. The Department of Justice had previously raised the alarm on an estimated 6 million fake PWD cards.

“Ang digital ID natin may unique QR Code po. So, iyong QR code po ii-scan lang ng ating mga merchants and then pag-scan didiretso po iyan sa government portal ng DSWD (Department of Social Welfare and Development), and then makikita po na verified iyong ating persons with disabilities. So ganoon lang kabilis po iyong pag-verify niya,” NCDA spokesperson Walter Jason Alava said on the Bagong Pilipinas Ngayon public briefing.

(Our digital ID has a unique QR code. So, this QR code can be scanned by merchants, which will go directly to a portal of the DSWD, then we can see the verified persons with disabilities. This makes it fast to verify.)
However, Alvava said that there is a Department of Justice (DOJ) opinion that stated that there should be a presumption of regularity

“Mayroon presumption of regularity kapag nag-present po ang ating mga person with disability ng kanilang identification. So, kailangan po bigyan natin sila ng discounts and then, kung nagdududa tayo ‘di ba na iyong person with disability, doon lang tayo magbi-verify,” the spokesperson said.

(There is a presumption of regularity if a person with disabilities presents identification. So we need to give them the discounts and then if we doubt the person with disability, that is when we verify.)
Alvava said that registration for the new digital ID is still in-person at local government units, as the council was still checking how to enhance an online registration system.
According to a Facebook post from the NCDA, a physical card may be printed upon request.

People with existing PWD cards only need to bring their IDs as long as they are still valid and unexpired. For first-time registrants, those who do not have an apparent disability must bring a certificate of disability from a licensed physician. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Sara Duterte received ‘return of capital’ of 2.14 million from GenCorp. — witness
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte has received a “return of capital” from a corporation tied to her, according to the fourth witness of the defense panel.

blocks.text: November 11, 2026 | 6:08pm
MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte has received a “return of capital” from a corporation tied to her, according to the fourth witness of the defense panel.

In her testimony, lawyer Suzette Balucanag-Punay, the in-house counsel of two corporations tied to the vice president, said that Duterte received a “return of capital” from GenCorp Industries Inc. from 2022 to 2025, amounting to P2.14 million.
According to Punay, citing company records, Duterte received disbursements of P555,750 in 2023, P612,419.14 in 2024 and P636,700 in 2025.
She also said that these disbursements were made through checks issued from a bank account belonging to Jollibee Times Square, which is tied to GenCorp.
Punay described the Vice President's financial interest as a "loose investment" tied specifically to a single branch, Jollibee Times Square, rather than equity in GenCorp itself.
“Even in Times Square branch, she has no involvement or participation,” Punay said.
Punay also said that Duterte has not received any dividends from the corporation, as it did not declare any.

Prosecution evidence shows that Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband, Manases Carpio, listed GenCorp Industries Inc., previously named Timesquare Bee Foods Corp. and Great Jolly Times Food, as a business interest in their joint SALNs for 2024 and 2025, as well as under its former name in her 2022 and 2023 filings.

Meanwhile, her brother, Davao City Mayor Sebastian "Baste" Duterte, testified before the impeachment court that while the city government awarded P33 million in contracts to GenCorp, he was unaware of his sister's connection to the company.

Article 7, Section 13 of the 1987 Constitution provides that the president, vice president, members of the Cabinet and their deputies or assistants shall not “hold any other office or employment during their tenure,” in order to avoid conflicts of interest.

It also prohibits these officials, during their tenure, from “directly or indirectly, practice any other profession, participate in any business, or be financially interested in any contract with, or in any franchise, or special privilege granted by the Government or any subdivision, agency, or instrumentality thereof, including government-owned or controlled corporations or their subsidiaries.”
Franchise history
Punay traced the history back to 2007, when Duterte was a stockholder in Davao Bounty Times Food Corp., according to her Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth.
She explained that Davao Bounty was originally incorporated to operate the Jollibee Times Square branch but failed to secure the franchise.
The franchise was instead granted to Great Jolly Times Foods Corporation, and Duterte's original investment was carried over.
Through a series of corporate transitions, the operations of the Times Square branch were eventually absorbed by GenCorp.
Punay asserted that because the original venture did not operate, the money being paid to Duterte is simply the return of her initial capital.
45 times higher

Senate Presiding Officer Francis Escudero pointed out that Duterte received P2.14 million from GenCorp between 2022 and 2025, about 45 times her documented P46,875 capital contribution to Davao Bounty Foods Corporation.
During the hearing, Escudero explained the difference between a return of investment and a return on investment.
Punay admitted that she could not explain how the payouts reached P2.14 million or point to additional investments justifying the total.
She eventually agreed with defense lawyer Lorna Kapunan that the sum represented earnings either way.
“Whether it be a return on investment or a return of investment, it is still income, correct?” Kapunan asked. To which Punay replied: “Yes.”
Punay is the fourth defense witness in Duterte’s impeachment trial under Article II of the Articles of Impeachment.
Article II covers allegations involving Duterte's alleged ill-gotten wealth and failure to fully disclose her assets and liabilities in her Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth.

articles.title: [Be The Good] Let’s not rely on Leni Robredo
articles.summary: When we look to one person, we miss the opportunity to cultivate a wider selection of politicians

blocks.text: She has spoken. The ship has sailed. Those hoping Naga City Mayor Leni Robredo would run for a national post in 2028 got a reality check on Monday, November 9. This whole fixation on Mayor Robredo though also got me thinking of a related issue: the shallow bench for alternative candidates.

When we look to one person, we miss the opportunity to cultivate a wider selection of politicians. Perhaps this decision of Robredo’s is a chance to widen our horizons and look to new faces. More importantly, it should allow us to examine ourselves. Quoting Mahatma Gandhi, should we not become the change we want to see?

I just came from a week in Cape Town, South Africa with Rappler’s scholars to the One Young World 2026 Summit. JJ Agustin, Gybel Agregado, Kit Posadas, John Mauro Manuel, and Jasser Mohammad are examples of young people who are becoming the change they want to see. They live it every day, in their work in youth political participation, agriculture, women empowerment, and data-driven storytelling. At the summit, which gathered 2,000 young people from over 190 countries, we listened to fellow youth leaders tell stories of the hardships they overcame, the challenges they continue to face, and the hope they keep alive for their communities and countries.
One speech at the summit resonated with me – that of Anna Strolenberg, who, at 31 years old, is one of the youngest members of the European Parliament.
Anna was recognized as one of the Politicians of the Year, an award given out at every One Young World Summit.
Like most of us, she used to think politics was a dirty word, “something for men with big egos and bad suits.”
But, when she was 24 years old, she decided to become a politician, not because she thought she’d be good at political maneuverings, but simply because she was fed up with the status quo.

“Many of you told me you have lost trust in politics because politicians are corrupt, or don’t represent you. And I want to tell you this: do not accept it. Go there yourself and make them change,” she said, to resounding applause.

I know many Filipinos don’t trust politics. Most of us are cynical, or have lost hope and have simply checked out. I get it. The headlines scream with reasons to be jaded: the massive flood control corruption, the poor services and facilities, the red tape and incompetence, the grandstanding with nothing to show for it. We rail against these failures of governance all the time. We are adept at outrage. If dissatisfaction with the status quo was a marathon, we would’ve won it a thousand times over.
But Anna said this cannot be enough.

“I have a warning, because our passion for protest doesn’t translate to a passion for politics. Young people have the most to gain, but by not being present, we accept that other people put us last,” she said.

Anna refused to accept this. Not even 30 years old, she set aside her nerves and doubts, and decided to join Volt Europa, a political party. The story of Volt is in itself striking. It was founded by three young people who met while studying at Columbia University and who decided they wanted to create a truly pan-European progressive political party that would push back against the nationalist, right-wing movements gaining ground in the region.
That was in 2017. Today, Volt has over 30,000 members from all over Europe, 400 members elected into office, including five in the European Parliament. Anna is one of those five.

“I know that politics is often a dirty word, but I think it’s up to us to change it. I am proud to say I’m a member of the European Parliament, that I’m changing politics – step by step, but I’m changing it,” said Anna at the One Young World Summit.

All over the world, we are seeing young people stepping out of their comfort zones, and getting some power in return. From France, to Nepal, to Bangladesh, to Serbia, youth-led protests and movements have sparked change, replaced regimes, or at the very least, catalyzed urgent conversations.

In the US, the youth vote played a decisive role in the blue wave that has given back power to the Democrats. Some 66% of voters aged 18 to 29 voted for Democratic candidates for the House of Representatives.

For sure, it is a difficult, even dangerous, road to take back power. In the Philippines, the electoral system is such that massive resources are needed to run for public office. But people with extremely limited resources can change the fate of a nation. South Africa gives us the best example. Nelson Mandela and his fellow freedom fighters against apartheid were facing deadly state force and next to no funding, not to mention a whole ecosystem of discriminatory laws, yet still managed to bring down the repressive system. It came at a great cost. But it was a cost they took on because the dream was worth it.
What dream for the Philippines is worth the cost? What cost are you willing to pay?

You can start by registering to vote in the 2028 elections, if you haven’t yet. Voter registration resumed on Monday, November 10 and will continue until July 30, 2027. You can register to vote at any Comelec office and certain malls, from 8 am to 5 pm. Here’s the directory of Comelec offices nationwide.

articles.title: Stellantis auto plant sale draws optimism, hurt in Brampton, Ont., after 2,000 jobs lost
articles.summary: Workers and local politicians are expressing disappointment at Stellantis's decision to sell its Brampton, Ont., plant to armoured vehicle maker Roshel Inc., but some local businesses and experts say…

image.caption: The Stellantis assembly plant in Brampton, Ont., has been purchased by Canadian armoured vehicle maker Roshel Inc. following a three-year shutdown, rattling autoworkers who lost their jobs. (Patrick Morrell/CBC)

blocks.text: Toronto·New

Workers and local politicians are expressing disappointment at Stellantis's decision to sell its Brampton, Ont., plant to armoured vehicle maker Roshel Inc., but some local businesses and experts say the new company could bring more jobs and foot traffic to the community.
Brampton Board of Trade hopes new owner means new jobs, investment, more local business
For three years, Shelly Lewis has been trying to increase foot traffic at her restaurant after it dwindled following the 2023 closure of the Stellantis auto plant in Brampton, Ont.

Shelly's Kitchen on Chrysler Drive is among the many food shops that relied on business from thousands of Stellantis workers, but Lewis said she's had to lay off a staff member and admits she has struggled to pay bills some months.
"The Stellantis plant made business for me because I had staff at all hours come in and I had lots of specials," she said. "I'm so sad that they shut down operations."
Now, however, she's hopeful that news the automater is expected to have a new owner will result in more customers at her eatery and rejuvenate the area.
On Monday, it was announced that Canadian armoured ⁠vehicle maker Roshel Inc. will buy the auto plant, acquiring the idled facility and equipment from Stellantis for an undisclosed amount.

items: Roshel to buy Stellantis assembly plant in Brampton for undisclosed amount, automaker says

blocks.text: That appears to be positive news, as more than 2,000 workers were laid off when operations were halted in in 2023 to retool the plant for Jeep production, a plan that was paused in early 2025.

Baltej Bajwa, among the over 2,000 workers laid off from Brampton's Stellantis facility, says it's great that Roshel is offering jobs to workers in the city, but fears there will be lots of uncertainty for colleagues. (CBC)
But Baltej Bajwa, one of the laid-off workers who's been left in limbo since the plant's closure, remains uncertain of his future and said he was shocked to hear about the sale.
"Any hope that we had of potentially coming back when we heard the news kind of just got shattered," Bajwa said.

items: How Pearson airport plans to fill jobs with laid-off Stellantis workers

blocks.text: Roshel Inc. CEO Roman Shimonov did say the company plans to employ thousands of people and will give first priority to the workers who lost their job in Brampton.
However, Bajwa said, Roshel's production capacity will be far fewer than the 400 to 800 vehicles that the 2,200 Stellantis workers produced daily.

"So yes, it's amazing that Roshel is giving us those job opportunities, but it still does kind of leave the other half of the plant in a state of disarray where we don't know where we're going to go."
'They can't cut and run,' mayor says
Roshel's purchase of the plant has garnered harsh words from union leaders and politicians.
Prime Minister Mark Carney called it a "betrayal" to all Canadians.
Lana Payne, national president of Unifor, said Monday that the sale is an "unacceptable outcome" for the union and its members, calling it the "worst-case scenario."

items: Stellantis auto plant closure in Brampton a 'betrayal' to all Canadians, Carney says

blocks.text: Brampton Mayor Patrick Brown echoed those sentiments. He said Stellantis has received "bailouts" from various levels of government over the years, including most recently in 2022, "on the basis of production in Canada."

"Brampton residents are rightfully angry. I think Canadians should be angry," he told CBC News on Tuesday. "This is a company that has depended on Canadian taxpayer generosity for decades. They can't cut and run without consequences.

"Stellantis has abandoned Canadian workers — they got bullied by the Trump administration. If we allow Stellantis to leave easily and ignore their legal obligations, this will not be the last auto plant that falls in Canada. Really, this is ground zero of protecting auto jobs."
In a statement, Stellantis said it would voluntarily repay the subsidies.
Purchase will drive up economic activity: Board of Trade
Brown said he thinks Roshel is a great local company that has ambitions to create thousands of jobs, but doesn't believe it should have purchased Stellantis.
However, Jaipaul Massey-Singh, CEO of the Brampton Board of Trade, believes this will be a boon to the city and the local economy.

He said the impact of Stellantis's closure goes beyond just workers, affecting their families and the local businesses they were supporting. He has heard from many shops that have laid off staff, lost orders and reduced their hours to stay afloat.

"Knowing that it's going to result in activity in that plant once more, creating employment for those who are going to be there but also additional employment and economic activity for the community in general, is absolutely welcome news," Massey-Singh said about the sale.

"For every employee that's affected, it's up to, five to six additional employees or workers in that community that are impacted. So in a place like Brampton, we're talking minimum [12,000] to 15,000 individuals who were impacted by Stellantis's decision to walk away."

The Chrysler Brampton Assembly plant is seen Nov. 10 in this image taken by drone. Local leaders have condemned Stellantis's decision to sell the plant, leaving over 2,000 workers without jobs. However, local businesses hope the sale will bring more foot traffic to the area. (Patrick Morrell/CBC)

Massey-Singh hopes every laid-off Stellantis employee gets their jobs back, and believes reopening the plant under new ownership will drive more investment and business in the form of new workers, retraining and additional resources.
Lewis remains optimistic that Roshel joining the community will help boost business for her restaurant and other local establishments.
"I'm happy that something else will be there again because they'll have people working there again and this plaza has lots of different businesses, so I know it's going to be better for everybody."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Isha Bhargava is a multiplatform reporter for CBC News in Peel Region where she covers everything from local news to current affairs and human interest stories. She was previously with CBC London. You can reach out to her with your story ideas at isha.bhargava@cbc.ca
With files from Dana Roberts, CBC News

articles.title: Congo's Ebola outbreak tops 11,000 cases as disease keeps spreading
articles.summary: The latest health ministry data Wednesday showed 11,042 people have been infected by the deadly virus that has now killed 5,387, nearly half of those infected, in the country's deadliest outbreak.

image.caption: A healthcare worker walks inside an Ebola treatment center in Beni, North Kivu Province, Congo, Monday, Nov. 9, 2026. (Sebastien Kitsa Musayi/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: Health·New
The latest health ministry data Wednesday showed 11,042 people have been infected by the deadly virus that has now killed 5,387, nearly half of those infected, in the country's deadliest outbreak.
The Bundibugyo virus responsible for this outbreak has no known vaccine or treatment

Congo's Ebola outbreak has topped 11,000 cases, the government said Wednesday, a stark figure that underscores the severity of the situation as the country grapples with the relentless spread of the disease.

According to the latest health ministry data, 11,042 people have been infected with the deadly virus that has now killed 5,387 — nearly half of those infected in what has been Congo's deadliest outbreak.

items: 'No one is safe' as Ebola outbreak surges to more than 10,000 cases, Africa's top doctor warns Canada

blocks.text: The outbreak was declared in mid-May, and since then, Congolese authorities have struggled to contain it due to several factors, including armed conflicts, a health system crisis, poor roads and violence from residents fueled by mistrust and misinformation.
The Bundibugyo virus responsible for this outbreak has no known vaccine or treatment and has spread to eight of the country's 26 provinces.
What Canadians should know about the Ebola outbreak

The resurgence of violence in the two major hotspots in Ituri and North Kivu provinces has sparked worry among health authorities who are calling for a halt to the fighting to allow health workers unhindered access to the sick.

items: Nigeria Ebola patient flown to Switzerland, Congo health worker killed as 4 countries deal with outbreak

blocks.text: Health facilities and medical professionals have also been targeted by many in communities skeptical of the virus, and there have been several attacks on health workers.
Experts have called for more efforts to slow and contain the disease in Congo, while it has spread to multiple African countries including Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria.

Dozens of Ebola outbreaks have been reported since the disease was first discovered in 1976. The largest and deadliest occurred in West Africa in 2014 to 2016, with 28,000 infections and more than 11,000 deaths.
The current outbreak already ranks second and has had at least three times the number of cases and deaths in the time since it was declared, compared with the West Africa outbreak.

articles.title: NAZA documentary on Gaza killings becomes one of year’s most watched
articles.summary:
The film, which details Israel’s surveillance of Palestinian civilians, has been seen by more than 1.5m people in less than two months

NAZA, the award-winning documentary that details…

blocks.text: NAZA, the award-winning documentary that details Israel’s mass killing of civilians in Gaza, has been seen by more than 1.5 million people since being released in cinemas across the world last month.

The film, which is directed by the Oscar-winning Israeli film-makers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor and produced by the Guardian, has reached a worldwide audience of 1,547,033 as of Friday 6 November, making it one of the most-watched documentary films with a theatrical release in 2026.

NAZA won the Special Jury prize at the Venice film festival in September, where its premiere was met with a record 24.5 minute standing ovation, and has received widespread critical acclaim. It drew worldwide attention after Israel’s culture minister threatened to strip its directors of their citizenship and prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered the identification and prosecution of the film’s interviewees.

After a cinematic run in 47 territories to date, the investigative documentary’s free global streaming release on theguardian.com is now planned for early December, as the Guardian works to prepare the online video release for a large global audience in multiple languages.

The film has already made cinematic history in Italy, where it was released in September. With 717,517 admissions, NAZA is the third most-watched documentary with a theatrical release of all time in Italy, behind Michael Moore’s Fahrenheit 9/11 and The March of the Penguins.

Other European regions with a notably large interest in NAZA include the UK and Ireland, where the film has garnered a total 102,508 admissions so far, and the Benelux, where distributor Cherry Pickers has counted 132,323 admissions across the three states Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg.

The film has clocked 83,673 admissions across the US and Canada, where it was initially released on 30 September through a self-release model but was picked up in October by distributor Neon. Earlier this month, it won the Critics’ Choice documentary award for best political documentary.

In France, NAZA has been shown in cinemas only over a limited 48-hour period due to the country’s strict rules around films that are also streamed online. The film nonetheless clocked up more than 82,000 admissions over nearly 500 screenings, ranking top of the box office on both days.

There have been multiple reports of audiences sitting in stunned silence as the film’s credits roll in cinemas. “Rarely does a film screening give way to such silence when the lights come back on,” said a review on Radio France.
after newsletter promotion
In Germany, where the war in Gaza and the government’s support of Israel have sown particularly deep division in the cultural scene, NAZA reached 83,355 spectators.

articles.title: Burnham lauds £12bn offshore wind investment as he prepares for climate summit
articles.summary: Project off Norfolk coast announced as government tries to calm critics after approving Jackdaw gasfield

blocks.text: Andy Burnham has hailed a record investment in offshore wind, as the government tries to repair its green credentials after approving the controversial Jackdaw gasfield in the North Sea.

On Wednesday the government announced a £12bn investment from the German energy company RWE and the US private equity firm KKR, as the prime minister prepares to travel to the Cop31 climate crisis summit in Turkey.
The investment package, which will go towards the creation of the Vanguard West and Vanguard East offshore windfarms off the Norfolk coast, is a “vote of confidence for building in Britain”, he said.
“It is great news for bill payers because every turbine we put up is power under British control, not at the mercy of events on the other side of the world.
“With coastal communities from Scotland to East Anglia powering Britain’s future, the places that host this energy benefit from the jobs and opportunities that it brings.”

blocks.caption: Andy Burnham has called the investment package a ‘vote of confidence for building in Britain’. Photograph: WPA/Getty Images

blocks.text: The offshore wind projects will also receive £1bn in funding from the state-owned national wealth fund.

The windfarms are set to be providing power by 2030, with construction set to begin early next year. The wind investment is “believed to be the biggest of its kind in UK history”, the government said.
RWE said the Vanguard project represents one of the UK’s largest offshore wind developments, generating about 2.8 gigawatts, enough to supply 3m homes.

It estimated that the construction of the windfarms will create and support 2,300 jobs each year through its supply chain. The windfarms are expected to create a further 100 long-term permanent jobs when they are operational.
The energy company SSE also announced on Wednesday that the latest phase of its major offshore windfarm, Berwick Bank B off the east coast of Scotland, would “support” 2,600 existing jobs.

Miatta Fahnbulleh, the energy secretary, said investment in offshore wind and clean power was “creating quality jobs and rebuilding industry, while delivering the clean power we need to lower bills and reach net zero”.
She added that Britain was “leading from the front as a renewable energy powerhouse”.
after newsletter promotion
It comes as Burnham seeks to bolster his government’s under-fire green credentials at Cop31, where he is expected to give a speech on Thursday.
The prime minister has faced a backlash from Labour MPs and environmental campaigners over his government’s decision to approve the Jackdaw gasfield.
On Tuesday, ministers also rejected plans to build what would have been Britain’s biggest solar plant near the Blenheim Palace estate.
Fahnbulleh turned down the £800m Botley West project, which would have covered almost 3,500 acres of land. Developers said it would have provided enough electricity to power 330,000 homes.

Margaret Curran, in a letter on behalf of the energy secretary, wrote that the project would cause “substantial harm” to the green belt and the Blenheim Estate – home to Blenheim Palace, which is a world heritage site and the birthplace of Winston Churchill.

articles.title: Tearful Smith switches allegiance to Netherlands
articles.summary: Tatjana Smith, South Africa's most decorated Olympian, switches allegiance to the Netherlands.

blocks.text: South Africa's most decorated Olympian Tatjana Smith was in tears as she announced that she has switched allegiance to the Netherlands.
The 29-year-old won four Olympic breaststroke medals, including two golds, before retiring after the Paris 2024 Games.
She came out of retirement in September and hopes to compete in the 50m breaststroke as the event makes its Olympic debut at the 2028 Games in Los Angeles.
Smith, whose maiden name was Schoenmaker, wiped away tears as she read a letter addressed to South Africa, saying that "dreams can change as we grow".
Smith has dual citizenship because her father is Dutch.
She said she has "always been Dutch and South African" and that this is an opportunity to "explore another part of my identity and heritage that I've never experienced through sport".

She said it also offers her "greater high-performance support and the potential to build a more sustainable career" because the "financial and practical challenges of swimming were among the reasons my previous career became difficult to sustain".
Smith has previously said that financial worries, which included a dispute with Swimming South Africa over prize money, contributed to her decision to step away from the sport.
Swimming South Africa has been approached for comment.
Smith won four world and Commonwealth gold medals between 2018 and 2023.
She won gold in the 200m breaststroke and 100m silver at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021, before adding 100m gold and 200m silver in 2024.
"Representing South Africa was a childhood dream come true, and it's a chapter I will always look back on with immense pride and gratitude," she said on social media., external
"The people, the memories and everything we achieved together will always be part of me. But dreams can change as we grow.
"This next chapter is about embracing another part of who I am, falling in love with the journey and discovering what more I'm capable of.
"I'm excited for what lies ahead, and I truly hope you'll continue to be part of the journey with me."
Smith, who said she will continue to live and train in South Africa, is set to represent the Netherlands for the first time at the short course World Championships from 1-6 December.
She acknowledged that her switch "may disappoint or break the hearts" of some supporters.
The Ministry of Sport, Arts and Culture in South Africa said it was aware of the "problems at Swimming South Africa".
"The country was delighted to see her return to the pool, but South Africa does not own her," a statement read.
"Tatjana's choice belongs to her and it should not be turned into a political weapon."
Gayton McKenzie, Minister of Sports, Arts and Culture, said: "Every medal, every record and every anthem she gave us belongs to our history forever. We now have to share her with the Netherlands."

articles.title: Macalintal files motion for partial reconsideration of SC BSKE ruling
articles.summary: Election lawyer Romulo Macalintal said that he filed a motion for partial reconsideration before the Supreme Court in relation to its ruling on the Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections (BSKE).

blocks.text: Published November 11, 2026 5:42pm
Election lawyer Romulo Macalintal said that he filed a motion for partial reconsideration before the Supreme Court in relation to its ruling on the Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections (BSKE).

Macalintal previously challenged the constitutionality of the newly signed Republic Act No. 12326, which extended the term of BSK officials, arguing it violated the people’s right to vote. However, the Supreme Court dismissed Macalintal’s petition, upholding the constitutionality of the law.

“The win-win solution respectfully submitted by the Petitioner is two-fold: first, to declare constitutional the power of Congress to extend the term of office of barangay and SK officials; and second, to declare unconstitutional—and/or violative of the 2023 Macalintal guidelines—the consequential postponement of the November 2026 BSKE,” Macalintal’s new petition read.
The Macalintal guidelines come from a 2023 decision from the Supreme Court that declared Republic Act No. 11935 — another law that postponed the BSKE — unconstitutional.

Macalintal said he conceded that Congress has the authority to enact legislation that extended the terms of BSKE officials; however, he asked the Supreme Court to reconsider its decision that the postponement is a mere “incident” of that power.

The petition asked the Supreme Court to direct the Commission on Elections “to conduct the Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections on the earliest practicable date, with the five-year term of office under Section 1 of Republic Act No. 12326 to apply to the officials elected therein and the next regular elections to be held five years thereafter.”
In a separate statement, Macalintal said that the proposed solution harmonized the interests of all the parties confirmed.

“Public respondents—Congress, the Office of the President, and the Commission on Elections—are sustained in their stance that Congress possesses the constitutional authority to determine terms of office. On the other hand, the Filipino electorate will rejoice as their sacred right of suffrage is fully restored and vindicated,” Macalintal said. –NB, GMA News

articles.title: Evidentiary weight of admission against interest discussed in Sara Duterte impeachment trial
articles.summary: Opinions clashed in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte on Wednesday on whether which has evidentiary weight between an admission against interest and official public documents.

blocks.text: Published November 11, 2026 5:32pm
Opinions clashed in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte on Wednesday on whether which has evidentiary weight between an admission against interest and official public documents.

Senator-judge Panfilo “Ping” Lacson raised the question on day 42 of the impeachment trial, directing it to Atty. Suzette Balucanag-Punay, in-house counsel for Gencorp Industries, Inc. and Metro City Chow Foods Corporation---the two entities linked to the Vice President.

“This is getting to be interesting, but also confusing. From a layman to a lawyer, Atty. Suzette, between an admission against interest--notarized--and official public documents like the GIS (General Information Sheet), which has more admissibility and probative weight?” Lacson asked.
Punay said she believes that records coming from the Securities and Exchange Commission have more probative weight.
Lacson countered, citing Rule 130 of the Rules of Court regarding the rules of admissibility.
“Alam ko po mas may probative weight or admissibility weight ‘yung admission against interest,” he said.
(As far as I know, an admission against interest carries greater probative weight or admissibility.)
“Meron nga akong kilala, sa TV lang nag-admit, nakulong eh. Ito, notarized pa itong [Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth],” he added.
(I actually know someone who ended up in jail just for making an admission on television. In this case, the SALN is involved.)
Impeachment court presiding officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero said the matter is subject to the appreciation of the senator-judges.
For his part, defense counsel Justin Gular said that an admission against interest is an exception to the hearsay rule.

“We have to be clear, Your Honor. Admission against interest is not a rule on probative value. It is an exception to the hearsay rule. In other words, comparing pieces of evidence and statements and the probative weight thereof, with all due respect, is done by the respective court and this case, the senator-judges,” Gular said.
Private prosecutor Lorna Kapunan, on the other hand, asserted that an admission is the “highest” in the hierarchy of evidence.
Citing the Rules of Court, Kapunan said that the act, declaration, or omission of a party as to a relevant fact may be given in evidence against him or her.
Escudero said both counsels have valid points.

“Nobody is wrong. Atty. Justin is correct that admission against interest is indeed an exception to the hearsay rule. Atty. Lorna is likewise correct that admission per se has been characterized in fact as the ‘queen of evidence,’ will carry more probative weight especially if it comes from the accused,” the presiding officer said. — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: Almost 1,600 cops sacked in PNP cleansing drive
articles.summary: More than 5,700 officers were penalized as a result of the PNP's latest cleansing drive, with absence without official leave cases resulting in the dismissal of 1,562.

blocks.text: November 11, 2026 | 5:23pm
Philippine National Police personnel
The Philippine STAR / Ryan Baldemor

MANILA, Philippines — Almost 6,000 personnel were penalized, including 1,562 officers who were dismissed from their positions, during an internal cleansing drive, the Philippine National Police announced on Wednesday, November 11.
The leading offense among those dismissed was absence without official leave, with 931 officers terminated for this reason.
Positive findings in illegal drug-related cases, meanwhile, resulted in the dismissal of 141 personnel, and robbery or extortion, the dismissal of 70 officers.
Cleansing initiatives, according to the PNP, form part of the police force's efforts to promote integrity.
Every police officer, Police General Jose Nartatez Jr. said, is expected to follow the same laws and standards the PNP is sworn to enforce.
Under Nartatez, the PNP has also set a "zero backlog" goal, with around 300,000 fugitives left on the force's list.
Among the high-profile personalities still being hunted by the PNP are Sen. Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa, who is wanted by the International Criminal Court for alleged crimes against humanity of murder.
Dela Rosa, having served as PNP chief during the term of former President Rodrigo Duterte, is accused of implementing Duterte's bloody war on drugs at a national level.

articles.title: Customs employee faces admin complaint after failing to file 2005 SALN
articles.summary: The Department of Finance"s (DOF) anti-corruption arm has filed an administrative complaint against a Bureau of Customs (BOC) employee after he failed to file his sworn Statement of Assets,…

blocks.text: Published November 11, 2026 5:18pm

The Department of Finance’s (DOF) anti-corruption arm has filed an administrative complaint against a Bureau of Customs (BOC) employee after he failed to file his sworn Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALN) for 2005.

DOF said the Civil Service Commission (CSC) National Capital Region confirmed that the required SALN was not in their records. CSC found the concerned BOC employee violated the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees.

“Failure to file a SALN cannot be taken lightly. This requirement exists to safeguard against corruption and the unlawful acquisition of wealth. DOF-RIPS will remain steadfast in pursuing administrative cases that help protect the integrity of government and uphold public trust,” said DOF Undersecretary Rolando Ligon Jr. in a statement.
Citing the Office of the Ombudsman, the CSC NCR noted that mandatory SALN filing protects against illegal wealth and corruption while reinforcing honesty in government service.

The CSC NCR imposed a suspension of three months and one day, which is the prescribed penalty for a first offense under Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees, the DOF said. —Vince Angelo Ferreras/RF, GMA News

articles.title: Burnham hails approval for two huge windfarm projects as ‘power under British control’ – UK politics live
articles.summary:
Announcement comes ahead of visit to Cop31 climate conference with PM also set to face MPs at PMQs

The CBI has issued a statement welcoming the PM’s offshore wind…

blocks.text: Key events

items: 13m agoEd Miliband says national security of all countries at risk from climate crisis
35m agoBurnham hails approval for two huge windfarm projects as ‘power under British control’

blocks.text: Ed Miliband says national security of all countries at risk from climate crisis

The national security of all countries is at risk from the climate crisis, as “science fiction” scenarios of widespread destruction are already coming true and economic shocks from fossil fuels are now the norm rather than the exception, Ed Miliband, the foreign secretary, will warn at the Cop31 summit today. Fiona Harvey has the story.
The CBI has issued a statement welcoming the PM’s offshore wind announcement. (See 8.55am.) This is from its chief executive, Rain Newton-Smith.

double quotation markThe prime minister’s announcement of major investment in offshore wind is a powerful restatement of the UK’s clean energy ambitions and the economic opportunities they can unlock. Investment on this scale can attract further private capital, create skilled jobs and support growth in communities across the country.
Burnham hails approval for two huge windfarm projects as ‘power under British control’

Good morning. Andy Burnham has got PMQs today, and after that he will leave for what looks like a rather hectic Turkey/Ireland trip which tomorrow will see him address the Cop31 climate summit in the morning, before attending his first major summit with EU leaders (and some other European leaders – it’s a European Political Community event) in Dublin later in the day.

Of the two events, the EPC is probably the more important for Burnham because it will give him the chance to clear the air ahead of the UK-EU summit next week, and because Burnham has made renegotiating the relationship with the EU a key aim of his premiership.

But Cop31 is important too because Burnham wants to show that he remains committed to the net zero climate agenda but that he is also “pragmatic” about pursuing this in a way that helps with cost of living pressures. This morning he has an announcement that will help in this respect; Downing Street has announced the next stage in two huge offshore wind projects.
One relates to the Vanguard East and Vanguard West projects. No 10 says:

double quotation markEnergy company RWE, together with global investment firm KKR, have announced a total investment of £12bn, believed to be the biggest of its kind in UK history to date. It will give the green light to its Vanguard West and Vanguard East offshore wind farms, set to be operational by 2030 and delivering clean, secure, homegrown power to homes and businesses that will protect families from global fossil fuel price shocks … On top of bolstering the UK’s green energy future, the investment will support more than 2,400 jobs during construction and operation, and once operational, the wind farms will have the capacity to supply the equivalent of around three million UK homes … The decision marks a major milestone for the project, with the developers now making their final investment commitment to deliver the projects. Onshore works are already well advanced, with construction offshore set to begin in early 2027.
The other relates to Berwick Bank B. No 10 says:

double quotation markOn top of this, Scottish-headquartered SSE has announced that the latest phase of its major offshore wind farm, Berwick Bank B, will back 2,677 skilled jobs in manufacturing, engineering and project delivery across the north of England and Scotland, with the company contracting Siemens Energy for the manufacturing of wind turbines and substation platforms. This includes the creation of 130 new project delivery roles in Glasgow and Montrose. At its full capacity, Berwick Bank, off the east coast of Scotland, could become the world’s largest offshore wind farm, capable of meeting more than 6% of current UK electricity demand.
Welcoming these announcements, Burnham said:

double quotation markThis major investment in UK renewables is a vote of confidence for building in Britain. And it is great news for billpayers because every turbine we put up is power under British control, not at the mercy of events on the other side of the world.
Ajit Niranjan has a separate live blog covering Cop31.
Here is the agenda for the day.
10am: Angela Rayner, the housing secretary, gives evidence to the Commons housing committee.
10.50am: Lucy Powell, the education secretary, gives a speech to the Association of Colleges annual conference in Birmingham.
11am: Louise Casey gives a speech at the National Children and Adult Services conference in Liverpool.
Noon: Andy Burnham faces Kemi Badenoch at PMQs.
Noon: Morgan McSweeney, Keir Starmer’s former chief of staff, gives evidence to the Lords constitution committee about constitutional safeguards.
1pm: Heidi Alexander, the transport secretary, gives a speech to the annual airlines’ conference in London.
2.15pm: John Healey, the chancellor, gives evidence to the Commons Treasury committee about the budget.
Afternoon: Burnham leaves London to fly to the Cop31 climate conference in Turkey.

articles.title: Spain: Housing crisis prompts general strike
articles.summary: Workers across nearly all industries have taken to the picket lines as rents soar and the housing crunch worsens. The crisis is the main political debate ahead of Spain's November 29 elections.

image.caption: The strike was led by CCOO and UGT, Spain's two largest unionsImage: Bruna Casas/REUTERS

blocks.text: Workers across Spain gathered en mass on Wednesday, marching and setting up picket lines despite stormy weather in many areas of the country.
This is the first general strike in Spain in 14 years, amid a worsening cost of living and lack of housing crisis that has left many unable to support themselves.
Symbolized by the eviction and death of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal in Madrid earlier this year, the crisis has also prompted a snap election set for November 29.

The government of left-wing Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez attempted to pass legislation to ease the plight of renters, but was blocked in parliament by opposition parties. Lacking the power to get legislation passed, Sanchez called the early vote in hopes to shore up more support.

"We won't stop until we transform this country's housing model from top to bottom so that houses are for living instead of being at the service of the [landlord] minority," said Alicia del Rio, spokesperson for the Madrid Tenants' Union.
87-year-old at heart of Spanish housing protests dies
How bad is Spain's housing crisis?
The country has a deficit of about 750,000 homes, which is set ​to grow to more than a million by 2028 according to estimates from the central bank.

With fewer and fewer individuals and families able to buy a home, the number of renters in the country has risen sharply. According to Spain's youth council, the average rent is €1,176 ($1,315). This is equivalent to 99% of the average young person's salary.

While most of the protests appeared to be proceeding peacefully, strikers in front of Madrid's Mercamadrid wholesale market said that police had fire pepper spray at the crowd, prompting at least 13 people to seek medical attention.

The general strike comes a day after rail workers launched a strike over two major deadly train crashes this year, making decrepit infrastructure also a major topic in the upcoming parliamentary elections.
Spain rail crash piles pressure on government before vote

articles.title: Ed Miliband says national security of all countries at risk from climate crisis
articles.summary: Exclusive: UK foreign secretary to tell world leaders at Cop31 summit that sci-fi scenarios of destruction ‘now regular occurrences’

blocks.text: The national security of all countries is at risk from the climate crisis, as “science fiction” scenarios of widespread destruction are already coming true and economic shocks from fossil fuels are now the norm rather than the exception, the UK’s foreign secretary is to warn world leaders gathered in Turkey on Wednesday.

Ed Miliband will tell the Cop31 UN climate summit that security and defence objectives are the new “frontier” of climate action, because the rapid heating of the planet will lead to food shortages, widespread economic disruption, migration and conflict.

“National security is the next frontier of the fight for climate action – the scenarios once of science fiction are now regular occurrences in the daily news,” Miliband told the Guardian ahead of his interventions before world leaders and governments in Antalya.

“We should be clear that climate breakdown is one of the greatest national security threats we face: food security, threats to infrastructure, and population movements [are resulting from the climate crisis],” he said.

blocks.caption: The Turkish president, Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, waters a newly planted olive sapling as the UN chief, António Guterres, and visiting world leaders look on. Photograph: Metin Aktas/Anadolu/Getty Images

blocks.text: In a veiled swipe at the Conservatives and Reform UK, which want to scrap efforts to cut greenhouse gas emissions, he added: “Those who seek to stick their heads in the sand on climate are putting our national security at risk.”
Miliband arrived in Turkey on Tuesday evening for the two-day leaders’ summit segment on Wednesday and Thursday of the fortnight-long Cop31 talks, which started on Monday.
Andy Burnham, the UK prime minister, is expected to travel on Wednesday for a series of bilateral meetings with fellow world leaders on Thursday.

Anthony Albanese, prime minister of Australia, and Turkish president, Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, will open the leaders’ summit segment on Wednesday, along with speeches by the UN secretary general António Guterres, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva of Brazil, which hosted last year’s Cop, and the prime minister of Ethiopia, Abiy Ahmed, who will host next year’s meeting.

However, the several heads of leading countries are skipping this year’s Cop, including China’s Xi Jinping, India’s Narendra Modi, France’s Emmanuel Macron and Germany’s Friedrich Merz. The European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, will attend.

Miliband will argue that the world must now face the consequences of failures to cut carbon emissions over the past three decades. “It is a disaster for people and the planet, and we must reckon with its implications,” he will tell audiences at Cop31 on Wednesday. “It will drive hardship and insecurity for billions of people.”

He will note that an “overshoot” of the crucial threshold of 1.5C of global heating, above preindustrial levels, is now inevitable, as temperatures have exceeded that level for two years and are unlikely to subside significantly. This “overshoot” requires stronger policies to ensure heating does not accelerate, and to seek ways of returning temperatures to safer levels in decades to come.
after newsletter promotion

blocks.caption: People wait to fill their tanks at a petrol station in Batangas, the Philippines. The war in the Middle East has hit global fuel prices. Photograph: Marc Dominic Rostrata/Zuma Press Wire/Shutterstock

blocks.text: Fossil fuel shocks, such as the soaring oil price seen this year following the Iran war, which has led to rampant inflation and interest rate rises from central banks in an effort to control it, will wreak further harm, according to Miliband.

He told the Guardian: “A new era of global insecurity means fossil fuel shocks are now the norm – the fossil fuel rollercoaster is here to stay. First Russia, now Iran, next others, have identified global chokepoints and systemic overreliance [on fossil fuels] and the vulnerability of countries around the world that they expose.”

He said the only answer was to “double down” on measures to cut greenhouse gas emissions and build resilience to the effects of extreme weather. “Next year will be the year of climate fightback, as governments, movements and communities across the world step up to defend our shared home.”

Miliband will call for more investment in clean energy and efforts to use it for transport and heating, as well as urgent action to cut methane, a powerful greenhouse gas, and protect and expand forests.

However, Burnham’s government is under fire in the UK for a series of recent and looming policy interventions that campaigners say will push the country off-track to meet its target of net zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050, and set a poor example to the rest of the world.

The government plans to weaken a mandate for carmakers to ensure more of their vehicles are electric by 2030, and has given the green light to a new gasfield, Jackdaw, in the North Sea, while considering licensing a new oilfield, Rosebank, west of Shetland.

articles.title: It’s official: SB19 is heading to Coachella 2027
articles.summary: 'We're doing this to help pave the way for more Filipino talent to be represented on the global stage. And we truly believe this is only the beginning,' Josh says about the group's latest feat

blocks.text: SB19. P-pop boy group SB19 will be performing at the 2027 edition of the Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival.
Kim Dominic via SB19's Facebook page
'We're doing this to help pave the way for more Filipino talent to be represented on the global stage. And we truly believe this is only the beginning,' Josh says about the group's latest feat

MANILA, Philippines – SB19 marks another milestone in its career as the Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival confirmed on Wednesday, November 11 (Manila time), that the P-pop boy group is on the lineup of its 2027 edition.

“From the very beginning, we’ve always dreamed of bringing Filipino music to places we once only imagined. To now have that dream become a reality, with A’TIN beside us every step of the way, is something we’ll never take for granted,” the group’s leader Pablo said about their inclusion in the upcoming festival, according to a press release.
“This one’s for everyone who believed in us from day one. Abangan kung ano ang pwedeng gawin ng SB dito (Watch out for what SB can do here)!”
Pablo, Stell, Justin, Ken, and Josh will be performing at Coachella on April 10 and 17, 2027. Other big names like Tame Impala, Phoebe Bridgers, and NCT will also be performing on the same dates.
Meanwhile, Filipino-American artist Steve Lacy, who earlier made his Manila debut at the LaLaLa Fest in August, is scheduled to take the stage on April 9 and 16.

“We hope this inspires the current and future generation of Filipino artists. Whether you’re part of a P-pop group or pursuing music and other creative fields, we want everyone to know that these opportunities are possible. We’re doing this to help pave the way for more Filipino talent to be represented on the global stage. And we truly believe this is only the beginning,” SB19’s Josh added.

In July, SB19 became the first all-Filipino group to perform at Lollapalooza, another major global music festival held annually in Chicago, Illinois. In the same month, the “GENTO” hitmakers were also named one of the Philippines’ official tourism ambassadors alongside P-pop girl group BINI.
In April this year, eight-member P-pop girl group BINI became the first homegrown Filipino act to appear at Coachella.

SB19’s inclusion in the 2027 Coachella lineup also comes after the “Kings of P-pop” wrapped up the sold-out “Wakas at Simula: The Trilogy Concert Finale at the SMDC Festival Grounds” in April. – Rappler.com
